source.text: Καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ· οὐ συμφέρον μέν, ἐλεύσομαι δὲ εἰς ὀπτασίας καὶ ἀποκαλύψεις κυρίου.

records.literal_gloss: To boast it is necessary; not profitable indeed, I will come but to visions and revelations of [the] Lord.

en.L: It is necessary to boast; it is not profitable, but I will go on to visions and revelations of [the] Lord.
en.B: I have to boast. It does no good, but now I will turn to visions and revelations given by the Lord.
en.R: I must go on boasting. It does not do any good, but I will do it. Now I will tell about visions and things the Lord has shown me.

fr.L: Il faut se vanter ; cela n’est pas utile, mais j’en viendrai aux visions et aux révélations du Seigneur.
fr.B: Il me faut me vanter. Cela ne sert à rien, mais j’en viens maintenant aux visions et aux révélations que le Seigneur a données.
fr.R: Je dois continuer à me vanter. Cela ne sert à rien, mais je vais le faire. Maintenant, je vais parler de visions et de choses que le Seigneur m’a montrées.

es.L: Es necesario gloriarse; no conviene, pero pasaré a [las] visiones y revelaciones del Señor.
es.B: Tengo que gloriarme. No sirve de nada, pero ahora pasaré a las visiones y revelaciones que el Señor me ha dado.
es.R: Tengo que seguir gloriándome. No sirve de nada, pero lo haré. Ahora voy a hablar de visiones y de cosas que el Señor me ha mostrado.

sw.L: Ni lazima kujivuna; haifai, lakini nitaendelea kwenye maono na mafunuo ya Bwana.
sw.B: Lazima nijivune. Haina faida, lakini sasa nitageukia maono na mafunuo aliyotoa Bwana.
sw.R: Ni lazima niendelee kujivuna. Haisaidii kitu, lakini nitafanya hivyo. Sasa nitawaeleza kuhusu maono na mambo ambayo Bwana amenionyesha.

vi.L: Cần phải khoe mình; điều đó chẳng có ích gì, nhưng tôi sẽ đi đến các khải tượng và sự mặc khải của Chúa.
vi.B: Tôi phải khoe mình. Điều đó chẳng ích lợi gì, nhưng bây giờ tôi sẽ nói đến các khải tượng và sự mặc khải Chúa ban cho.
vi.R: Tôi phải tiếp tục khoe mình. Điều đó chẳng ích lợi gì, nhưng tôi sẽ làm. Bây giờ tôi sẽ kể về các khải tượng và những điều Chúa đã tỏ cho tôi.

ko.L: 자랑해야 합니다. 유익하지는 않지만, 주님의 환상들과 계시들로 넘어가겠습니다.
ko.B: 나는 자랑해야 합니다. 아무 유익이 없지만, 이제 주님께서 주신 환상과 계시를 이야기하겠습니다.
ko.R: 나는 계속 자랑해야 합니다. 그것이 아무 도움이 되지 않지만, 그렇게 하겠습니다. 이제 내가 본 환상들과 주님께서 나에게 보여 주신 것들을 이야기하겠습니다.

decisions.choice: it is necessary to boast: Paul is pushed into boasting by the situation in Corinth
alternatives: boasting is a duty in itself
decisions.reason: Καυχᾶσθαι δεῖ ("to boast is necessary") picks up the boasting Paul began in 11:16-33, the "fool's speech" he takes up against his rivals. The necessity is not a rule but the pressure of the moment: in 12:11 he says the Corinthians forced him to it, because they did not speak up for him.

decisions.choice: not profitable: boasting does no real good
decisions.reason: οὐ συμφέρον means "not beneficial, not useful". Paul grants that boasting builds no one up (compare 12:19, where all he does is for their building up), yet he goes on because the situation demands it.

decisions.choice: visions and revelations from the Lord: given by the Lord
alternatives: visions and revelations in which the Lord is seen
decisions.reason: The genitive κυρίου ("of [the] Lord") most naturally names the giver: the Lord granted these experiences. It could also include the Lord as what was seen, and the two senses overlap. "Lord" here is most likely Christ, as in 12:8-9.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "it is necessary to boast; it is not profitable, but I will go on"
alternatives: later manuscripts: "boasting is not profitable for me, for I will go on"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the first words of the verse: many later manuscripts read a particle instead of δεῖ, add "for me" and join the clauses differently, which is the reading of the King James Version. The meaning is close either way. The SBLGNT text is followed. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: boast (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: In 2 Corinthians 10-12 Paul's argument turns on the word itself, so all three levels keep "boast" here and through the chapter, as the book-wide choice for these chapters settles.

decisions.choice: Now I will tell about visions and things the Lord has shown me
alternatives: I will go on to visions and revelations of the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable explains "revelations" as things the Lord has shown and says that Paul is moving to a new subject.

decisions.choice: se vanter at every level (for chapters 10-12)
decisions.reason: In Paul's fool's speech the argument turns on the word itself, and the English keeps "boast" at all three levels here. "Se vanter" is the French word with the same edge as "boast", and it keeps Paul's irony audible; "se glorifier" would sound too solemn for a speech Paul calls foolish; Literal uses "se vanter" across 1 and 2 Corinthians in any case.

decisions.choice: gloriarse at every level
decisions.reason: As in chapters 10-11 (decision at 10:8), Paul's ironic boasting carries the argument, so every level keeps "gloriarse".

decisions.choice: kujivuna at every level
decisions.reason: As set in 10:8 for chapters 10-12, the boasting verb stays "kujivuna" / "kujivunia" at every level, as the English keeps "boast".

decisions.choice: "các khải tượng và sự mặc khải của Chúa" (L); "... Chúa ban cho" (B); "những điều Chúa đã tỏ cho tôi" (R)
alternatives: "sự hiện thấy và sự tỏ ra"
decisions.reason: Given by the Lord (m3, uncertain). "Sự mặc khải" is the word of the Vietnamese Galatians 1:12 and Ephesians 1:17 for apokalypsis.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình" at every level, as in chapters 10-11
decisions.reason: Paul is pushed into boasting (m1); the chapters 10-12 choice.

decisions.choice: "환상", "계시" (L, B); "환상", "주님께서 보여 주신 것" (R)
decisions.reason: Plain Korean words; the meaning decision reads "of the Lord" as naming the giver, so Basic and Readable say "주님께서 주신", "보여 주신".

decisions.choice: Literal follows the SBLGNT, "자랑해야 합니다. 유익하지는 않지만"
decisions.reason: Follows the SBLGNT reading set by the meaning decision.

source.text: οἶδα ἄνθρωπον ἐν Χριστῷ πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων εἴτε ἐν σώματι οὐκ οἶδα, εἴτε ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν ἁρπαγέντα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἕως τρίτου οὐρανοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: I know a man in Christ before years fourteen, whether in [the] body not I know, or outside of the body not I know, the God knows, having been caught up the such [one] up to [the] third heaven.

en.L: I know a man in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, fourteen years ago (whether in [the] body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know; God knows), such a [man] caught up as far as [the] third heaven.
en.B: Fourteen years ago a man I know, a man in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, was snatched away as far as the third heaven. Whether this happened in the body or outside the body, I do not know. God knows.
en.R: I know a man who belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Fourteen years ago he was taken up into the third heaven. I do not know if he was in his body or out of his body when it happened. Only God knows.

fr.L: Je connais un homme {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, [il y a] quatorze ans (soit dans le corps, je ne sais pas, soit hors du corps, je ne sais pas ; Dieu sait), un tel [homme] enlevé jusqu’au troisième ciel.
fr.B: Il y a quatorze ans, un homme que je connais, un homme {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, a été enlevé jusqu’au troisième ciel. Cela s’est-il passé dans son corps ou hors de son corps, je ne le sais pas. Dieu le sait.
fr.R: Je connais un homme qui appartient au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Il y a quatorze ans, il a été emporté jusqu’au troisième ciel. Je ne sais pas s’il était dans son corps ou hors de son corps quand c’est arrivé. Dieu seul le sait.

es.L: Conozco a un hombre en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} que hace catorce años (si en [el] cuerpo, no lo sé; si fuera del cuerpo, no lo sé; Dios lo sabe) fue arrebatado, el tal, hasta [el] tercer cielo.
es.B: Hace catorce años, un hombre que conozco, un hombre en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, fue arrebatado hasta el tercer cielo. Si esto ocurrió en el cuerpo o fuera del cuerpo, no lo sé. Dios lo sabe.
es.R: Conozco a un hombre que pertenece {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Hace catorce años fue llevado al tercer cielo. No sé si estaba en su cuerpo o fuera de su cuerpo cuando sucedió. Solo Dios lo sabe.

sw.L: Ninamfahamu mtu aliye katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, ambaye miaka kumi na minne iliyopita (ikiwa alikuwa mwilini, sijui; ikiwa nje ya mwili, sijui; Mungu ndiye ajuaye), mtu wa namna hiyo alinyakuliwa mpaka mbingu ya tatu.
sw.B: Miaka kumi na minne iliyopita, mtu mmoja ninayemfahamu, mtu aliye katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, alinyakuliwa mpaka mbingu ya tatu. Kama jambo hilo lilitokea akiwa katika mwili au nje ya mwili, sijui. Mungu anajua.
sw.R: Ninamfahamu mtu mmoja aliye wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Miaka kumi na minne iliyopita alichukuliwa juu mpaka mbingu ya tatu. Sijui kama alikuwa ndani ya mwili wake au nje ya mwili wake wakati jambo hilo lilipotokea. Mungu peke yake ndiye anajua.

vi.L: Tôi biết một người ở trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, mười bốn năm trước (hoặc trong thân thể, tôi không biết, hoặc ngoài thân thể, tôi không biết; Đức Chúa Trời biết), người ấy đã được cất lên đến tầng trời thứ ba.
vi.B: Mười bốn năm trước, có một người tôi biết, một người ở trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, đã được cất lên đến tận tầng trời thứ ba. Việc ấy xảy ra trong thân thể hay ngoài thân thể, tôi không biết. Đức Chúa Trời biết.
vi.R: Tôi biết một người thuộc về {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Mười bốn năm trước, người ấy được đem lên tầng trời thứ ba. Tôi không biết lúc đó người ấy ở trong thân thể hay ở ngoài thân thể. Chỉ có Đức Chúa Trời biết.

ko.L: 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있는 한 사람을 압니다. 그는 십사 년 전에—몸 안에 있었는지 나는 모릅니다. 몸 밖에 있었는지도 나는 모릅니다. 하나님께서 아십니다— 그런 사람이 셋째 하늘까지 이끌려 올라갔습니다.
ko.B: 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에 있는 한 사람을 압니다. 십사 년 전에 그 사람은 셋째 하늘까지 이끌려 올라갔습니다. 그것이 몸 안에서 일어난 일인지 몸 밖에서 일어난 일인지 나는 모릅니다. 하나님께서 아십니다.
ko.R: 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께 속한 한 사람을 압니다. 십사 년 전에 그는 셋째 하늘로 들려 올라갔습니다. 그 일이 일어났을 때 그가 몸 안에 있었는지 몸 밖에 있었는지 나는 모릅니다. 오직 하나님께서만 아십니다.

decisions.choice: a man in Christ: Paul is speaking of himself in the third person
decisions.reason: Verse 7 shows that the man is Paul: the revelations were so great that he himself was given a thorn to keep him humble. He speaks of "a man" to keep the experience at a distance, as something given to him and not an achievement he can take credit for (verse 5). ἄνθρωπον here is one particular man, not people in general. "In Christ" means a believer, one who belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: fourteen years ago: counted back from the time of writing
decisions.reason: πρὸ ἐτῶν δεκατεσσάρων counts back from when Paul writes. If 2 Corinthians was written in the mid-50s, the experience falls in the early 40s, years before Paul came to Corinth. The Corinthians had evidently never heard of it, which shows how little Paul made of it.

decisions.choice: the third heaven: the highest heaven, where God is
alternatives: one of seven heavens, not the highest
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of the time could speak of several heavens, above the sky and the stars. Here "the third heaven" is the highest one, the place of God's presence, and verse 4 calls the same place paradise. Some Jewish texts count seven heavens, but nothing in the passage suggests Paul means a lower level.

decisions.choice: caught up: suddenly seized and carried away by God's power
decisions.reason: ἁρπαγέντα is a passive of the verb for snatching or seizing. The same verb is used for believers being caught up to meet the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:17) and for Philip being carried away by the Spirit (Acts 8:39). Paul did not ascend by his own effort; he was taken.

decisions.choice: whether in the body or outside the body: Paul does not know how it happened
alternatives: Paul denies that the body was involved
decisions.reason: The repeated οὐκ οἶδα ("I do not know") and ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν ("God knows") interrupt the sentence. Paul is sure of the experience but not of its manner, whether he was taken bodily or only in spirit, and he leaves that to God.

decisions.choice: a man, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The word refers to one particular man, Paul himself (m1), so it takes no gender setting.

decisions.choice: Fourteen years ago a man I know ... was snatched away as far as the third heaven. Whether this happened ...
alternatives: keeping the interruption in the middle of the sentence
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the main statement first and the interruption about the body after it, so that the sentence can be followed when read aloud.

decisions.choice: passé composé at every level, the account of the vision included ("a été enlevé")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("fut enlevé")
decisions.reason: 2 Corinthians is a letter, and past events are in the passé composé at every level, as in Colossians. Paul does not narrate the vision step by step here; he tells the readers what he knows about a man and what happened to him, so the speech tense is kept.

decisions.choice: alinyakuliwa (L, B); alichukuliwa juu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kunyakuliwa" is to be snatched up suddenly, carried away by a power not one's own (meaning decision); Readable says plainly "alichukuliwa juu" (was taken up). "Mtu" needs no gender span, as the English has none.

decisions.choice: "một người", "người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Paul is speaking of himself in the third person (m1); Vietnamese "người" already covers it, as the English has no setting here.

decisions.choice: "được cất lên đến tầng trời thứ ba" (L, B); "được đem lên tầng trời thứ ba" (R) for harpazo
decisions.reason: Suddenly seized and carried away by God's power (m4), to the highest heaven, where God is (m3); "được cất lên" is the form of the Vietnamese 1 Thessalonians 4:17.

decisions.choice: "한 사람" at every level, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has no gender setting: Paul speaks of himself in the third person, and Korean "사람" says it.

decisions.choice: "이끌려 올라가다" (L, B); "들려 올라가다" (R); "셋째 하늘"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as being seized and carried away by God's power; the passive Korean verb keeps God as the unnamed actor.

decisions.choice: The aside "몸 안에 ... 하나님께서 아십니다" set off with dashes (L)
decisions.reason: Brackets in Literal mark supplied words only.

source.text: καὶ οἶδα τὸν τοιοῦτον ἄνθρωπον εἴτε ἐν σώματι εἴτε χωρὶς τοῦ σώματος οὐκ οἶδα, ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν ὅτι ἡρπάγη εἰς τὸν παράδεισον καὶ ἤκουσεν ἄρρητα ῥήματα ἃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀνθρώπῳ λαλῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And I know the such man, whether in [the] body or apart from the body not I know, the God knows, \v 4 that he was caught up into the paradise and heard unspeakable words which not being permitted for a man to speak.

en.L: And I know such a man (whether in [the] body or apart from the body I do not know; God knows), \v 4 that he was caught up into paradise and heard unutterable words, which a human being is not allowed to speak.
en.B: This same man, I know (in the body or apart from it, I do not know; God knows), \v 4 was snatched away into paradise. There he heard things beyond speaking, which no human being is allowed to tell.
en.R: I also know this about that man. I do not know if he was in his body or out of it; God knows. \v 4 But I know that he was taken up into paradise. There he heard things too holy to put into words, things no person is allowed to repeat.

fr.L: Et je sais d’un tel homme (soit dans le corps, soit sans le corps, je ne sais pas ; Dieu sait) \v 4 qu’il a été enlevé au paradis et a entendu des paroles inexprimables, qu’il n’est pas permis à un être humain de dire.
fr.B: Cet homme-là, je le connais (dans son corps ou sans son corps, je ne sais pas ; Dieu le sait), \v 4 et il a été enlevé jusqu’au paradis. Là, il a entendu des choses qu’on ne peut exprimer, qu’aucun être humain n’a le droit de redire.
fr.R: Je sais aussi ceci au sujet de cet homme. Je ne sais pas s’il était dans son corps ou hors de son corps ; Dieu le sait. \v 4 Mais je sais qu’il a été emporté au paradis. Là, il a entendu des choses trop saintes pour être dites avec des mots, des choses que personne n’a le droit de répéter.

es.L: Y conozco a tal hombre (si en [el] cuerpo o fuera del cuerpo, no lo sé; Dios lo sabe), \v 4 que fue arrebatado al paraíso y oyó palabras inefables, que no le está permitido a un ser humano pronunciar.
es.B: Y sé que este mismo hombre (en el cuerpo o fuera de él, no lo sé; Dios lo sabe) \v 4 fue arrebatado al paraíso. Allí oyó cosas que no se pueden expresar, que a ningún ser humano le está permitido contar.
es.R: Sé también esto acerca de ese hombre. No sé si estaba en su cuerpo o fuera de él; Dios lo sabe. \v 4 Pero sé que fue llevado al paraíso. Allí oyó cosas demasiado santas para expresarlas con palabras, cosas que a nadie le está permitido repetir.

sw.L: Nami ninamfahamu mtu huyo (ikiwa katika mwili au bila mwili, sijui; Mungu anajua), \v 4 kwamba alinyakuliwa mpaka paradiso, akasikia maneno yasiyoweza kutamkwa, ambayo mwanadamu haruhusiwi kuyasema.
sw.B: Mtu huyo huyo, namfahamu (kama ni katika mwili au bila mwili, sijui; Mungu anajua), \v 4 alinyakuliwa mpaka paradiso. Huko alisikia mambo yasiyoweza kusemwa, ambayo hakuna mwanadamu anayeruhusiwa kuyasimulia.
sw.R: Ninajua pia jambo hili kuhusu mtu huyo. Sijui kama alikuwa ndani ya mwili wake au nje yake; Mungu anajua. \v 4 Lakini najua kwamba alichukuliwa juu mpaka paradiso. Huko alisikia mambo matakatifu mno yasiyoweza kuelezwa kwa maneno, mambo ambayo hakuna mtu anayeruhusiwa kuyarudia.

vi.L: Và tôi biết người như thế (hoặc trong thân thể, hoặc ngoài thân thể, tôi không biết; Đức Chúa Trời biết), \v 4 rằng người ấy đã được cất lên đến Ba-ra-đi và nghe những lời không thể nói ra, là những lời mà loài người không được phép nói.
vi.B: Tôi biết chính người này (trong thân thể hay ngoài thân thể, tôi không biết; Đức Chúa Trời biết) \v 4 đã được cất lên đến Ba-ra-đi. Ở đó người ấy nghe những điều không thể diễn tả, là những điều không một con người nào được phép nói ra.
vi.R: Tôi còn biết điều này về người ấy. Tôi không biết người ấy ở trong thân thể hay ở ngoài thân thể; Đức Chúa Trời biết. \v 4 Nhưng tôi biết người ấy đã được đem lên thiên đàng. Ở đó người ấy nghe những điều quá thánh khiết đến nỗi không thể nói thành lời, những điều không ai được phép nhắc lại.

ko.L: 그리고 나는 그런 사람을 압니다—몸 안에 있었는지 몸 밖에 있었는지 나는 모릅니다. 하나님께서 아십니다— \v 4 그는 낙원으로 이끌려 올라가서, 말할 수 없는 말을 들었는데, 그것은 사람이 말해서는 안 되는 것입니다.
ko.B: 이 사람을 나는 압니다. (몸 안에서인지 몸 밖에서인지 나는 모릅니다. 하나님께서 아십니다.) \v 4 그는 낙원으로 이끌려 올라가서 말로 다 할 수 없는 일들을 들었습니다. 그것은 어떤 사람에게도 말하도록 허락되지 않은 것들입니다.
ko.R: 또 나는 그 사람에 대해 이것을 압니다. 그가 몸 안에 있었는지 몸 밖에 있었는지 나는 모릅니다. 하나님께서 아십니다. \v 4 그러나 나는 그가 낙원으로 들려 올라갔다는 것을 압니다. 그곳에서 그는 너무 거룩해서 말로 옮길 수 없는 것들을 들었습니다. 그것은 어떤 사람도 다시 말해서는 안 되는 것들입니다.

decisions.choice: the same experience told a second time
decisions.reason: Verses 3-4 repeat the wording of verse 2 almost exactly, with the same interruption about the body. The repetition is solemn emphasis, and "paradise" names the same place as "the third heaven". Some have read two stages of one journey, but nothing in the text marks a second event.

decisions.choice: paradise: the place of God's presence and blessing
alternatives: a place of the dead below the earth
decisions.reason: παράδεισον is a word borrowed from Persian for a walled park or garden. The Greek Old Testament uses it for the garden of Eden (Genesis 2:8), and in Jewish hope it came to mean the place where God's people are with him. Jesus promises it to the man crucified with him (Luke 23:43), and Revelation 2:7 places the tree of life there.

decisions.choice: unutterable words: things that cannot and may not be spoken
decisions.reason: ἄρρητα can mean "too sacred to be spoken" or "beyond words". The relative clause ἃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἀνθρώπῳ λαλῆσαι ("which it is not permitted for a human being to speak") shows the stress falls on what is forbidden: Paul was not allowed to repeat what he heard. So he can boast of the experience but cannot use its content to impress anyone.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "apart from"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read ἐκτὸς, the word used in verse 2, instead of χωρὶς. The meaning is the same. The SBLGNT text is followed. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: things beyond speaking
decisions.reason: "Things" suits English better than "words" here, since what Paul heard is the content of a revelation; "beyond speaking" keeps both sides of the word (m3).

decisions.choice: I also know this about that man ... But I know that ... things too holy to put into words
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the sentence up and says why the words cannot be repeated: they are too holy (m3).

decisions.choice: je sais d’un tel homme ... qu’il a été enlevé
alternatives: je connais un tel homme ... [je sais] qu’il a été enlevé
decisions.reason: The same verb governs both the man and the clause that follows. French "savoir de quelqu’un que" lets Literal keep one verb for both, without a supplied word.

decisions.choice: "Ba-ra-đi" (L, B); "thiên đàng" (R) for paradeisos
decisions.reason: The place of God's presence and blessing (m2); the forms of the Vietnamese Luke 23:43.

decisions.choice: "những lời không thể nói ra" (L); "những điều không thể diễn tả" (B); "quá thánh khiết đến nỗi không thể nói thành lời" (R)
decisions.reason: Things that cannot and may not be spoken (m3).

decisions.choice: "낙원" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as the place of God's presence and blessing.

decisions.choice: "말할 수 없는 말" (L); "말로 다 할 수 없는 일들" (B); "너무 거룩해서 말로 옮길 수 없는 것들" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as things that cannot and may not be spoken.

decisions.choice: "사람" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" includes women and men.

decisions.choice: "몸 밖에" (L, B, R), as in verse 2
decisions.reason: Follows the SBLGNT "apart from"; Korean has one plain phrase for both Greek words.

source.text: ὑπὲρ τοῦ τοιούτου καυχήσομαι, ὑπὲρ δὲ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ καυχήσομαι εἰ μὴ ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις.

records.literal_gloss: On behalf of the such [one] I will boast, on behalf of but myself not I will boast except in the weaknesses.

en.L: On behalf of such a [man] I will boast, but on behalf of myself I will not boast, except in [my] weaknesses.
en.B: About a man like that I will boast, but about myself I will boast only of my weaknesses.
en.R: I will boast about that man. When it comes to myself, the only things I will boast about are my weaknesses.

fr.L: Au sujet d’un tel [homme] je me vanterai, mais au sujet de moi-même je ne me vanterai pas, sinon de [mes] faiblesses.
fr.B: D’un homme comme celui-là, je me vanterai, mais de moi-même, je ne me vanterai que de mes faiblesses.
fr.R: Je me vanterai au sujet de cet homme. Mais quand il s’agit de moi, les seules choses dont je me vanterai, ce sont mes faiblesses.

es.L: De tal [hombre] me gloriaré, pero de mí mismo no me gloriaré, sino en [mis] debilidades.
es.B: De un hombre así me gloriaré, pero de mí mismo solo me gloriaré de mis debilidades.
es.R: Me gloriaré de ese hombre. En cuanto a mí, de lo único que me gloriaré es de mis debilidades.

sw.L: Kwa ajili ya mtu wa namna hiyo nitajivuna, lakini kwa ajili yangu mwenyewe sitajivuna, isipokuwa katika udhaifu [wangu].
sw.B: Kuhusu mtu kama huyo nitajivuna, lakini kuhusu nafsi yangu sitajivunia kitu isipokuwa udhaifu wangu.
sw.R: Nitajivuna kuhusu mtu huyo. Lakini kuhusu mimi mwenyewe, mambo pekee nitakayojivunia ni udhaifu wangu.

vi.L: Về người như thế, tôi sẽ khoe mình, nhưng về chính tôi, tôi sẽ không khoe mình, ngoại trừ về những sự yếu đuối [của tôi].
vi.B: Về một người như vậy, tôi sẽ khoe mình, nhưng về chính mình, tôi chỉ khoe về những sự yếu đuối của tôi.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ khoe mình về người ấy. Còn về chính tôi, điều duy nhất tôi sẽ khoe là những sự yếu đuối của tôi.

ko.L: 이런 사람을 위해서는 내가 자랑하겠지만, 나 자신을 위해서는 [나의] 약함 외에는 자랑하지 않겠습니다.
ko.B: 그런 사람에 대해서는 내가 자랑하겠습니다. 그러나 나 자신에 대해서는 내 약함밖에 자랑하지 않겠습니다.
ko.R: 나는 그 사람에 대해서는 자랑하겠습니다. 그러나 나 자신에 대해서는 내 약함만 자랑하겠습니다.

decisions.choice: boasting about "such a man" but not about "myself": the same person seen two ways
decisions.reason: The man of verses 2-4 is Paul (verse 7), so the contrast is not between two people. Paul will boast of what was given to the man in Christ, because it was God's gift and nothing he did. About himself, as the Corinthians see him, he will boast only of weakness.

decisions.choice: weaknesses: the limits, hardships and humiliations of Paul's life
decisions.reason: ἀσθενείαις covers being weak in every sense: bodily frailty, suffering and lack of standing. The list Paul has just given in 11:23-33, ending with his escape in a basket, shows what he means. These are the things his rivals despise (10:10) and the things through which Christ's power works (12:9).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the weaknesses", with no "my"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts add "my" after "weaknesses". The sense is the same, since Paul is speaking of his own weaknesses. The SBLGNT text is followed. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: [my] weaknesses (L); my weaknesses (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek article here points to Paul's own weaknesses, which English says with "my".

decisions.choice: "[của tôi]" (L); "của tôi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has "the weaknesses" with no "my" (m3); the English supplies it, and so does the Vietnamese, since Paul means his own.

decisions.choice: "약함" at every level, as at 11:30
decisions.reason: The key word of verses 5-10, kept the same.
Follows the SBLGNT, which has no "my"; the English supplies it.

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ θελήσω καυχήσασθαι, οὐκ ἔσομαι ἄφρων, ἀλήθειαν γὰρ ἐρῶ· φείδομαι δέ, μή τις εἰς ἐμὲ λογίσηται ὑπὲρ ὃ βλέπει με ἢ ἀκούει τι ἐξ ἐμοῦ, καὶ τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῶν ἀποκαλύψεων.

records.literal_gloss: If for I should want to boast, not I will be a fool, truth for I will speak; I refrain but, lest anyone to me credit beyond what he sees me or hears anything from me, \v 7 and by the surpassingness of the revelations.

en.L: For if I should want to boast, I will not be a fool, for I will be speaking [the] truth; but I refrain, so that no one may credit to me more than what {{gender:they see|he sees}} in me or {{gender:hear|hears}} from me, \v 7 even because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations.
en.B: Should I decide to boast, that would not make me a fool, since it would be the truth I spoke. But I hold back. I do not want anyone to think more of me than what {{gender:they see|he sees}} in me or {{gender:hear|hears}} from me, \v 7 or to think more of me because the revelations were so extraordinary.
en.R: If I chose to boast, I would not really be a fool, because everything I said would be the truth. But I will not do it. I do not want people to think more of me than what they see me do and hear me say. \v 7 And I do not want them to think more of me because the things God showed me were so amazing.

fr.L: Car si je voulais me vanter, je ne serais pas insensé, car je dirais la vérité ; mais je m’en abstiens, afin que personne ne m’attribue plus que ce qu’il voit en moi ou ce qu’il entend de moi, \v 7 et à cause de la grandeur extraordinaire des révélations.
fr.B: Si je décidais de me vanter, je ne serais pas insensé pour autant, puisque ce serait la vérité que je dirais. Mais je me retiens. Je ne veux pas qu’on se fasse de moi une idée plus haute que ce qu’on voit en moi ou ce qu’on m’entend dire, \v 7 ni qu’on m’estime davantage parce que les révélations étaient si extraordinaires.
fr.R: Si je choisissais de me vanter, je ne serais pas vraiment insensé, car tout ce que je dirais serait vrai. Mais je ne le ferai pas. Je ne veux pas que les gens pensent plus de bien de moi que ce qu’ils me voient faire et m’entendent dire. \v 7 Et je ne veux pas qu’ils pensent plus de bien de moi parce que les choses que Dieu m’a montrées étaient si extraordinaires.

es.L: Porque si quisiera gloriarme, no seré insensato, pues diré [la] verdad; pero me abstengo, para que nadie me atribuya más de lo que ve en mí u oye de mí, \v 7 aun por la grandeza extraordinaria de las revelaciones.
es.B: Si decidiera gloriarme, no por eso sería un insensato, porque diría la verdad. Pero me contengo. No quiero que nadie piense de mí más de lo que ve en mí o me oye decir, \v 7 ni que piense más de mí porque las revelaciones fueron tan extraordinarias.
es.R: Si yo quisiera gloriarme, en realidad no sería un tonto, porque todo lo que dijera sería verdad. Pero no lo voy a hacer. No quiero que la gente piense de mí más de lo que me ve hacer y me oye decir. \v 7 Y no quiero que piensen más de mí porque las cosas que Dios me mostró fueron tan asombrosas.

sw.L: Kwa maana nikitaka kujivuna, sitakuwa mpumbavu, kwa maana nitasema kweli; lakini najizuia, mtu yeyote asinidhanie kuwa zaidi ya kile anachoniona au anachosikia kutoka kwangu, \v 7 hata kwa sababu ya ukuu upitao kiasi wa mafunuo.
sw.B: Nikiamua kujivuna, hilo halitanifanya mpumbavu, kwa kuwa nitakuwa nasema kweli. Lakini najizuia. Sitaki mtu yeyote anifikirie kuwa zaidi ya anavyoniona au anavyosikia kutoka kwangu, \v 7 wala anifikirie kuwa zaidi kwa sababu mafunuo yale yalikuwa ya ajabu mno.
sw.R: Kama ningechagua kujivuna, kwa kweli nisingekuwa mpumbavu, kwa sababu kila ningesema kingekuwa kweli. Lakini sitafanya hivyo. Sitaki watu wanifikirie kuwa zaidi ya wanavyoniona nikitenda na wanavyonisikia nikisema. \v 7 Wala sitaki wanifikirie kuwa zaidi kwa sababu mambo ambayo Mungu alinionyesha yalikuwa ya ajabu sana.

vi.L: Vì nếu tôi muốn khoe mình, tôi sẽ không phải là người ngu dại, vì tôi sẽ nói sự thật; nhưng tôi tránh [điều đó], để không ai kể tôi hơn điều người ấy thấy nơi tôi hay nghe từ tôi, \v 7 dù là vì sự lớn lao vượt bậc của các sự mặc khải.
vi.B: Nếu tôi quyết định khoe mình, thì điều đó cũng không làm tôi thành người ngu dại, vì điều tôi nói là sự thật. Nhưng tôi kiềm chế. Tôi không muốn ai nghĩ về tôi hơn những gì người ấy thấy nơi tôi hay nghe từ tôi, \v 7 hoặc nghĩ về tôi cao hơn vì các sự mặc khải ấy quá phi thường.
vi.R: Nếu tôi chọn khoe mình, tôi cũng sẽ không thật sự là người ngu dại, vì mọi điều tôi nói đều là sự thật. Nhưng tôi sẽ không làm điều đó. Tôi không muốn người ta nghĩ về tôi cao hơn những gì họ thấy tôi làm và nghe tôi nói. \v 7 Và tôi không muốn họ nghĩ về tôi cao hơn vì những điều Đức Chúa Trời đã tỏ cho tôi quá kỳ diệu.

ko.L: 내가 자랑하려고 해도 어리석은 사람이 되지 않을 것입니다. 내가 진실을 말할 것이기 때문입니다. 그러나 나는 그만두겠습니다. 누가 나에게서 보거나 나에게서 듣는 것보다 나를 더 높이 여기지 않게 하려는 것이고, \v 7 계시들이 엄청나게 크기 때문에도 [그렇습니다].
ko.B: 내가 자랑하기로 한다 해도 어리석은 사람이 되지는 않을 것입니다. 내가 말하는 것은 진실일 것이기 때문입니다. 그러나 나는 그만두겠습니다. 나는 누구든지 나에게서 보거나 듣는 것보다 나를 더 높이 생각하지 않기를 바랍니다. \v 7 계시들이 너무나 놀랍다고 해서 나를 더 높이 생각하지 않기를 바랍니다.
ko.R: 내가 자랑하기로 한다 해도 정말로 어리석은 사람이 되지는 않을 것입니다. 내가 하는 말은 모두 진실일 것이기 때문입니다. 그러나 나는 그렇게 하지 않겠습니다. 나는 사람들이 내가 하는 일을 보고 내가 하는 말을 듣는 것보다 나를 더 높이 생각하지 않기를 바랍니다. \v 7 그리고 하나님께서 나에게 보여 주신 것들이 너무나 놀랍다고 해서 사람들이 나를 더 높이 생각하지 않기를 바랍니다.

decisions.choice: not a fool, because it would be true: boasting of real revelations would not be folly
decisions.reason: In 11:16-12:10 Paul speaks "as a fool", boasting in the way his rivals do. Here he says that if he chose to boast of experiences like these, he would not really be a fool, because everything he said would be true. The word ἄφρων ("fool") is the same one he uses of his whole speech in 11:16-19 and 12:11.

decisions.choice: I refrain: Paul wants to be judged only by what people can see and hear
alternatives: he is afraid of being disbelieved
decisions.reason: φείδομαι means "I spare, I hold back". λογίσηται is to reckon something to someone's account. Paul does not want anyone to credit him with more than his visible life and his preaching show. Visions cannot be checked, and his rivals evidently built their standing on such claims.

decisions.choice: the phrase about the revelations ends verse 6's sentence, as in the SBLGNT
alternatives: it begins the next sentence: "And because of the surpassing greatness of the revelations, therefore, so that I would not become proud, I was given a thorn"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a full stop after καὶ τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῶν ἀποκαλύψεων ("and by the surpassing greatness of the revelations"), so the phrase finishes verse 6: no one should think more of Paul because of the revelations. Many editions and translations instead begin verse 7 with it: the greatness of the revelations is why the thorn was given. That reading makes the διὸ ("therefore") after it awkward, which is one reason some manuscripts leave that word out (see the next sentence). Either way the revelations are the occasion of the thorn. The evidence is close, so this is uncertain.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they see|he sees}}, {{gender:hear|hears}}
decisions.reason: τις ("anyone") means any person, man or woman, so the pronoun goes through the gender setting. Readable says "people" and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: or to think more of me because the revelations were so extraordinary
alternatives: and by the surpassing greatness of the revelations
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out how the phrase joins the sentence on the SBLGNT reading (m3).

decisions.choice: insensé at every level (as in the fool's speech of chapter 11)
decisions.reason: "Fou" in French mostly means mad, which is the sense of another word in 11:23 ("out of my mind"). "Insensé" is a person without good sense, the part Paul says he is playing.

decisions.choice: personne ... ce qu’il voit (L); on (B), with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:they see|he sees}} for the pronoun after "anyone". French "personne ... il" and "on" are already generic and take no span, as the style guide asks.

decisions.choice: nadie ... ve ... oye, with no gender setting
alternatives: a gender setting as in the English
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender setting for "they see|he sees"; the Spanish verbs carry no pronoun, so "nadie ... ve ... oye" already includes women and men.

decisions.choice: anachoniona, anachosikia, no gender span
decisions.reason: The Swahili verb prefix "a-" is he or she alike, so the English gender spans have nothing to change in Swahili.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người ấy" is already man or woman.

decisions.choice: the phrase about the revelations ends verse 6's sentence
decisions.reason: As in the SBLGNT and the English (m3, uncertain).

decisions.choice: "누가 ... 보거나 ... 듣는" (L, B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "누가" and "누구든지" include women and men; the English Literal and Basic gender spans have no Korean counterpart.

decisions.choice: Literal keeps the phrase about the revelations at the end of verse 6's sentence, as in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision's punctuation.

source.text: διὸ ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι, ἐδόθη μοι σκόλοψ τῇ σαρκί, ἄγγελος Σατανᾶ, ἵνα με κολαφίζῃ, ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore so that not I may be exalted, was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan, so that me he may beat, so that not I may be exalted.

en.L: Therefore, so that I would not exalt myself, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan, to beat me, so that I would not exalt myself.
en.B: So, to stop me from becoming too proud, a thorn in the flesh was given to me: a messenger of Satan, sent to beat me down, to stop me from becoming too proud.
en.R: That is why I was given a painful thorn in my flesh. It was a messenger from Satan, sent to keep hitting me, so that I would not become too proud.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, afin que je ne m’enorgueillisse pas, une écharde dans la chair m’a été donnée, un messager de Satan, pour me frapper, afin que je ne m’enorgueillisse pas.
fr.B: Aussi, pour m’empêcher de devenir trop orgueilleux, une écharde dans la chair m’a été donnée : un messager de Satan, envoyé pour me rouer de coups, pour m’empêcher de devenir trop orgueilleux.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que j’ai reçu une écharde douloureuse dans ma chair. C’était un messager de Satan, envoyé pour me frapper sans cesse, pour que je ne devienne pas trop fier.

es.L: Por lo cual, para que no me enalteciera, me fue dada una espina en la carne, un mensajero de Satanás, para que me abofeteara, para que no me enalteciera.
es.B: Por eso, para que no me volviera demasiado orgulloso, se me dio una espina clavada en la carne: un mensajero de Satanás, enviado para golpearme, para que no me volviera demasiado orgulloso.
es.R: Por eso se me dio una espina dolorosa clavada en mi carne. Era un mensajero de Satanás, enviado para golpearme una y otra vez, para que no me volviera demasiado orgulloso.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, nisije nikajikweza, nilipewa mwiba ndani ya mwili, mjumbe wa Shetani, ili anipige ngumi, nisije nikajikweza.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, ili nisiwe na kiburi kupita kiasi, nilipewa mwiba katika mwili: mjumbe wa Shetani, aliyetumwa kunipiga na kunishusha, ili nisiwe na kiburi kupita kiasi.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu nilipewa mwiba unaouma katika mwili wangu. Ulikuwa mjumbe kutoka kwa Shetani, aliyetumwa kunipiga tena na tena, ili nisiwe na kiburi.

vi.L: Vì vậy, để tôi khỏi tự tôn mình lên, đã có một cái gai trong xác thịt được ban cho tôi, là một sứ giả của Sa-tan, để đánh tôi, để tôi khỏi tự tôn mình lên.
vi.B: Cho nên, để tôi khỏi trở nên quá kiêu ngạo, một cái gai trong xác thịt đã được ban cho tôi: một sứ giả của Sa-tan được sai đến để đánh gục tôi, để tôi khỏi trở nên quá kiêu ngạo.
vi.R: Vì thế tôi đã bị ban cho một cái gai nhức nhối trong thân thể. Đó là một sứ giả từ Sa-tan, được sai đến để cứ đánh tôi mãi, hầu cho tôi khỏi trở nên quá kiêu ngạo.

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 스스로 높아지지 않도록 나에게 육체의 가시, 곧 사탄의 사자가 주어졌습니다. 나를 치게 하여 내가 스스로 높아지지 않게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그래서 내가 너무 교만해지지 않도록 나에게 육체의 가시가 주어졌습니다. 그것은 나를 쳐서 쓰러뜨리려고 보낸 사탄의 사자입니다. 내가 너무 교만해지지 않게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.R: 그래서 나에게 몸을 찌르는 아픈 가시가 주어졌습니다. 그것은 사탄에게서 온 사자였는데, 나를 계속 치려고 보내진 것입니다. 내가 너무 교만해지지 않게 하려는 것이었습니다.

decisions.choice: a thorn in the flesh: some painful, lasting trouble; what it was is not known
decisions.reason: σκόλοψ is a pointed stake or a splinter, here a picture of something that kept piercing Paul. He does not say what it was, and the Corinthians may have known. Proposals include an illness or disability (in Galatians 4:13-15 an illness brought him to Galatia and the Galatians would have given him their eyes; Galatians 6:11 mentions his large letters), his opponents and persecution (in Numbers 33:55 enemies left in the land are "thorns in your sides"), and inner temptation. The last fits poorly with something that humbled him through weakness. The text does not decide, so the rendering keeps Paul's own picture.

decisions.choice: was given: God gave it, though it was a messenger of Satan
decisions.reason: The passive ἐδόθη ("was given") is the way Scripture often speaks of what God does, and the purpose clauses ("so that I would not exalt myself") are God's purpose, not Satan's. As with Job (Job 1-2), Satan means harm, but God uses it for good: here, to keep Paul humble. Satan would hardly aim to stop Paul from being proud.

decisions.choice: a messenger of Satan: an agent sent by Satan
decisions.reason: ἄγγελος means a messenger, human or angelic, and is the usual word for an angel. In apposition to the thorn it names the trouble as Satan's attack. Whether Paul means a personal evil spirit, hostile people, or speaks in a picture cannot be settled, and the rendering "messenger" leaves this open.

decisions.choice: to beat: to strike with the fist, again and again
decisions.reason: κολαφίζῃ is to strike with the fist, as Jesus was struck at his trial (Mark 14:65) and as Paul was treated (1 Corinthians 4:11). The present tense suggests repeated or continuing blows.

decisions.choice: so that I would not exalt myself: to keep Paul from becoming proud
alternatives: so that others would not exalt me
decisions.reason: ὑπεραίρωμαι means to lift oneself up too high, to become arrogant. The clause comes at the beginning and again at the end of the sentence, which stresses the purpose. Some manuscripts do not have the second one.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "therefore" at the start, and the purpose clause twice
decisions.reason: Some important early manuscripts have διὸ ("therefore") and others, with many later manuscripts, leave it out; leaving it out makes it easy to begin the sentence with the end of verse 6 (see the punctuation decision there). Some manuscripts also lack the second ἵνα μὴ ὑπεραίρωμαι. The SBLGNT text is followed. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a thorn in the flesh
decisions.reason: Paul's own picture is kept, because what it stood for is unknown (m1), and "thorn in the flesh" has become an English phrase for a lasting trouble.

decisions.choice: a painful thorn in my flesh
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and adds "painful" and "my" so a young reader sees that it hurt Paul himself, without saying what it was.

decisions.choice: become too proud; beat me down
decisions.reason: Balanced uses plain words for being lifted up in pride and for the repeated blows (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: une écharde dans la chair; un messager de Satan
decisions.reason: "Une écharde" is the splinter that lodges under the skin and keeps hurting, and "une écharde dans la chair" is the established French phrase for a lasting trouble, so Paul's picture is kept without saying what it was (m1). "Ange" would suggest a heavenly being; the sense is an agent sent by Satan (m3).

decisions.choice: espina
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a pointed stake or thorn, as the English says "thorn". "Aguijón" is the traditional Spanish but names an insect's sting; "espina" keeps the picture of something sharp lodged in the body.

decisions.choice: nisije nikajikweza (L); nisiwe na kiburi (B, R)
decisions.reason: This verb is lifting oneself up in pride (meaning decision). "Kujivuna" is kept for the boasting word that runs through chapters 10-12, so Literal says "kujikweza" (to exalt oneself) and Balanced and Readable "kuwa na kiburi" (to become proud).

decisions.choice: anipige ngumi
decisions.reason: "Kupiga ngumi" is to strike with the fist, the sense of the verb (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say it plainly.

decisions.choice: "một cái gai trong xác thịt" (L, B); "một cái gai nhức nhối trong thân thể" (R)
decisions.reason: Some painful, lasting trouble whose nature is not known (m1, uncertain); Literal and Balanced keep "xác thịt" so the reader can trace the Greek, Readable says "thân thể" because the trouble is bodily or close to it.

decisions.choice: "được ban cho tôi" (L, B); "tôi đã bị ban cho" (R)
decisions.reason: God gave it, though it was a messenger of Satan (m2); the passive is kept, so God is the giver.

decisions.choice: "sứ giả của Sa-tan" (L, B), "sứ giả từ Sa-tan" (R); "đánh" (L), "đánh gục" (B), "cứ đánh tôi mãi" (R)
decisions.reason: An agent sent by Satan (m3); striking with the fist, again and again (m4).

decisions.choice: "육체의 가시" (L, B); "몸을 찌르는 아픈 가시" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the thorn as some painful, lasting trouble whose nature is not known; "육신" in this project names human weakness or sinful nature, so the plain "육체" (the body) is used.

decisions.choice: "사탄의 사자" (L, B); "사탄에게서 온 사자" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as an agent sent by Satan; "사자" is the word for a messenger.

decisions.choice: "스스로 높아지다" (L), twice; "너무 교만해지다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as lifting oneself too high; Literal keeps the purpose clause twice, as in the SBLGNT.

decisions.choice: "주어졌습니다" (L, B, R), a passive with no named giver
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the passive as God's doing; Korean keeps the Greek's restraint.

source.text: ὑπὲρ τούτου τρὶς τὸν κύριον παρεκάλεσα ἵνα ἀποστῇ ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Concerning this three times the Lord I begged that it might depart from me;

en.L: Concerning this I appealed to the Lord three times, that it might depart from me.
en.B: I begged the Lord three times about this, asking that it would leave me.
en.R: I asked the Lord three times to make it go away.

fr.L: À ce sujet, trois fois j’ai supplié le Seigneur, pour qu’elle s’éloigne de moi.
fr.B: J’ai supplié le Seigneur à trois reprises à ce sujet, en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandant qu’elle me quitte.
fr.R: Trois fois, j’ai demandé au Seigneur de me l’enlever.

es.L: Acerca de esto tres veces rogué al Señor que se apartara de mí.
es.B: Tres veces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogué al Señor por esto, pidiéndole que se apartara de mí.
es.R: Tres veces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pedí al Señor que me la quitara.

sw.L: Kuhusu jambo hili nilimsihi Bwana mara tatu, ili liniondokee.
sw.B: Nilimsihi Bwana mara tatu kuhusu jambo hili, nikiomba liniache.
sw.R: Nilimwomba Bwana mara tatu aliondoe.

vi.L: Về điều này, đã ba lần tôi nài xin Chúa để nó lìa khỏi tôi.
vi.B: Đã ba lần tôi nài xin Chúa về điều này, xin cho nó rời khỏi tôi.
vi.R: Tôi đã ba lần xin Chúa cất nó đi.

ko.L: 이것에 대해 나는 그것이 나에게서 떠나게 해 달라고 주님께 세 번 간구했습니다.
ko.B: 나는 이것을 없애 달라고 주님께 세 번 간청했습니다.
ko.R: 나는 주님께 그것을 없애 달라고 세 번 부탁했습니다.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Christ
decisions.reason: The answer in verse 9 speaks of "my power" and Paul then calls it "the power of Christ", so the Lord Paul prayed to is the risen Christ. This is one of the places where Paul speaks of praying to Christ.

decisions.choice: appealed: pleaded, earnestly asked
decisions.reason: παρεκάλεσα is the verb that means "comfort" in 1:3-7 and 7:6-7. Here, with an object and a request, it has its other common sense: to call on someone, to plead with him.

decisions.choice: three times: three separate, earnest prayers
decisions.reason: τρὶς most likely means three distinct times of prayer. Jesus also prayed three times in Gethsemane that the cup might pass (Mark 14:32-41), and his request too was answered with something other than removal, but Paul makes no reference to that.

decisions.choice: it: the thorn, also called a messenger of Satan
alternatives: he: the messenger as a person
decisions.reason: τούτου and the subject of ἀποστῇ ("might depart") can be read as "this one" (the messenger) or "this thing" (the thorn). They are the same trouble seen in two ways, so the meaning does not change.

decisions.choice: appealed
decisions.reason: Literal uses a word that fits a prayer (m2); the family is rendered "comfort" only where it means comfort.

decisions.choice: qu’elle s’éloigne, qu’elle me quitte
decisions.reason: "It" is the thorn (m4). French agrees the pronoun with "écharde", which is feminine; "il" could be read as the Lord or as the messenger.

decisions.choice: "nài xin" (L, B); "xin" (R) for parakaleo here
decisions.reason: Pleaded, earnestly asked (m2); here the verb is prayer to the Lord, Christ (m1).

decisions.choice: "간구하다" (L); "간청하다" (B); "부탁하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as pleading with the Lord; "간구하다" is the word for earnest prayer.

source.text: καὶ εἴρηκέν μοι· Ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου· ἡ γὰρ δύναμις ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ τελεῖται.

records.literal_gloss: And he has said to me, "Suffices for you the grace of me; the for power in weakness is brought to completion."

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has said to me, "My grace is sufficient for you, for power is brought to completion in weakness."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me, "My grace is enough for you, for power comes to its fullness in weakness."
en.R: But the Lord answered me, "My grace is enough for you. Power does its greatest work where there is weakness."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : « Elle te suffit, ma grâce ; car la puissance est portée à son achèvement dans la faiblesse. »
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a répondu : « Ma grâce est tout ce qu’il te faut, car c’est dans la faiblesse que la puissance atteint sa plénitude. »
fr.R: Mais le Seigneur m’a répondu : « Ma grâce, c’est tout ce dont tu as besoin. La puissance agit pleinement là où il y a de la faiblesse. »

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me ha dicho: «Te basta {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gracia, porque el poder se perfecciona en [la] debilidad».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} me respondió: «Mi gracia te basta, porque el poder llega a su plenitud en la debilidad».
es.R: Pero el Señor me respondió: «Mi gracia es suficiente para ti. El poder hace su mayor obra donde hay debilidad».

sw.L: Naye ameniambia, "Neema {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inakutosha, kwa maana nguvu hufikia ukamilifu wake katika udhaifu."
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alinijibu, "Neema {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inakutosha, kwa maana nguvu hufikia utimilifu wake katika udhaifu."
sw.R: Lakini Bwana alinijibu, "Neema {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inakutosha. Nguvu hufanya kazi yake kubwa zaidi pale palipo na udhaifu."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán với tôi: "Ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đủ cho con, vì quyền năng được làm cho trọn vẹn trong sự yếu đuối."
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lời tôi: "Ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đủ cho con, vì quyền năng được trọn vẹn trong sự yếu đuối."
vi.R: Nhưng Chúa đáp lời tôi: "Ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là đủ cho con. Quyền năng làm công việc lớn lao nhất ở nơi có sự yếu đuối."

ko.L: 그러자 그분은 나에게 말씀하셨습니다. "나의 은혜가 너에게 족하다. 능력은 약함 안에서 온전해지기 때문이다."
ko.B: 그러나 주님께서는 나에게 대답하셨습니다. "나의 은혜가 너에게 충분하다. 능력은 약함 속에서 완전하게 드러나기 때문이다."
ko.R: 그러나 주님께서는 나에게 대답하셨습니다. "나의 은혜면 너에게 충분하다. 능력은 약함이 있는 곳에서 가장 큰 일을 한다."

decisions.choice: has said: an answer given once that still stands
decisions.reason: εἴρηκέν is in the perfect tense: the Lord gave his answer, and it remains his word to Paul. The thorn was not taken away; the answer replaced the request.

decisions.choice: my grace is enough: the Lord's favor and help are all Paul needs
alternatives: grace as an inner strength apart from Christ
decisions.reason: Ἀρκεῖ means "is enough, is sufficient". χάρις is the Lord's undeserved favor, which in Paul includes his active help (1 Corinthians 15:10: "by the grace of God I am what I am"). The speaker is Christ (verse 8), so it is Christ's grace.

decisions.choice: power is brought to completion in weakness: power does its full work where human strength fails
decisions.reason: τελεῖται means to complete, to carry through to its goal. The power is the Lord's (verse 9b names it "the power of Christ"). It reaches its full effect in weakness, where nothing human can take the credit, as the clay pots of 4:7 show.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "power", with no "my"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "my" ("my power"), the reading of the King James Version. The SBLGNT text has none. The sense is little affected, since the next sentence calls it the power of Christ. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the Lord Christ. "My" at the start of his words is capitalized in any case and needs no setting; Readable says "the Lord".

decisions.choice: grace
decisions.reason: Grace is a key term and keeps its word at every level.

decisions.choice: is enough; comes to its fullness (B); does its greatest work (R)
decisions.reason: "Made perfect" can suggest moral perfection; Balanced and Readable say that power reaches its full effect (m3).

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, the Lord of verse 8.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} for the Lord, subject included; "Ma" at the start of his words with no span
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the New Testament in French, every pronoun for Christ carries the span, subject "il" included. "Ma" opens the quoted sentence and is capitalised either way.

decisions.choice: « Elle te suffit, ma grâce »
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "suffices" first, and the French dislocation keeps that stress natural at Literal.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gracia
decisions.reason: The Lord speaks of his own grace, and the Spanish already drafted puts the deity_pronoun setting on "mi" when God or Christ speaks. At Balanced and Readable "Mi" begins the quotation and is capitalised either way, so it is written plain, as a sentence-initial pronoun is.

decisions.choice: Naye (L, no span); {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} (B); {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Lord speaks of himself, so his "yangu" (my) takes the span at every level, as the Swahili style guide says. At Literal "Naye" begins the sentence and is written plainly with its capital; Balanced has the free pronoun "yeye", which takes the span.

decisions.choice: "Ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đủ cho con", with "con" for Paul
decisions.reason: The Lord's favor and help are all Paul needs (m2). The Lord speaks to one servant, so "con", as when God speaks to one person in the Old Testament quotations of these letters.

decisions.choice: "được làm cho trọn vẹn" (L); "được trọn vẹn" (B); "làm công việc lớn lao nhất" (R) for teleitai
decisions.reason: Power does its full work where human strength fails (m3).

decisions.choice: The Lord's words in the plain style with "너" ("족하다", "때문이다")
decisions.reason: Jesus' words are in 해라체, as settled for the Gospels and in 1 Corinthians 11:24-25.

decisions.choice: "족하다" (L); "충분하다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as "is enough, is sufficient".

decisions.choice: "온전해지다" (L); "완전하게 드러나다" (B); "가장 큰 일을 한다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as carrying through to its goal: power does its full work where human strength fails.

decisions.choice: "능력" with no "my" (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Follows the SBLGNT.

decisions.choice: "그분은 ... 말씀하셨습니다" (L); "주님께서는" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean uses "그분" or the title, with no span (docs/korean-style.md).

source.text: ἥδιστα οὖν μᾶλλον καυχήσομαι ἐν ταῖς ἀσθενείαις μου, ἵνα ἐπισκηνώσῃ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ ἡ δύναμις τοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Most gladly therefore rather I will boast in the weaknesses of me, so that may tent upon me the power of the Christ.

en.L: Most gladly, therefore, I will rather boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} may pitch [its] tent over me.
en.B: So I will be all the happier to boast of my weaknesses, for then the power of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} may spread its tent over me.
en.R: So I am very glad to boast about my weaknesses. Then the power of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will stay over me like a tent.

fr.L: Très volontiers donc je me vanterai plutôt de mes faiblesses, afin que la puissance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} dresse [sa] tente sur moi.
fr.B: Je me vanterai donc d’autant plus volontiers de mes faiblesses, car alors la puissance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} pourra étendre sa tente sur moi.
fr.R: Alors je suis très content de me vanter de mes faiblesses. Ainsi, la puissance du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} restera sur moi comme une tente.

es.L: Con muchísimo gusto, pues, me gloriaré más bien en mis debilidades, para que el poder del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} plante [su] tienda sobre mí.
es.B: Por eso, con mayor alegría me gloriaré de mis debilidades, para que el poder {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} extienda su tienda sobre mí.
es.R: Así que me alegra mucho gloriarme de mis debilidades. Entonces el poder {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} se quedará sobre mí como una tienda de campaña.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo kwa furaha kubwa zaidi nitajivunia zaidi udhaifu wangu, ili nguvu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ipige hema juu yangu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nitafurahi zaidi kujivunia udhaifu wangu, ili nguvu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} itande hema yake juu yangu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo ninafurahi sana kujivunia udhaifu wangu. Ndipo nguvu ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} itakaa juu yangu kama hema.

vi.L: Vậy, tôi sẽ rất vui lòng khoe mình về những sự yếu đuối của tôi thì hơn, để quyền năng của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} dựng lều trên tôi.
vi.B: Vì thế, tôi lại càng vui mừng khoe mình về những sự yếu đuối của tôi, vì khi đó quyền năng của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} có thể giăng lều che phủ tôi.
vi.R: Vậy tôi rất vui được khoe mình về những sự yếu đuối của tôi. Khi đó quyền năng của {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} sẽ ở trên tôi như một cái lều che chở.

ko.L: 그러므로 나는 오히려 매우 기쁘게 나의 약함을 자랑하겠습니다. {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력이 내 위에 장막을 치게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 더욱 기쁘게 내 약함을 자랑하겠습니다. 그러면 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력이 장막처럼 내 위에 펼쳐질 것입니다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 아주 기쁘게 내 약함을 자랑합니다. 그러면 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}의 능력이 천막처럼 내 위에 머물 것입니다.

decisions.choice: most gladly, rather: instead of asking for the weakness to go, Paul will boast of it
decisions.reason: ἥδιστα is "most gladly". μᾶλλον ("rather") sets this against his prayer in verse 8: instead of begging to be rid of weakness, he will boast of it. It may also mean "all the more"; the point is the same.

decisions.choice: may pitch its tent over me: may come to dwell on me and shelter me
decisions.reason: ἐπισκηνώσῃ is built on the word for a tent and means to take up lodging, to dwell. The picture is of Christ's power settling over Paul as a dwelling and a shelter.

decisions.choice: the tent may recall God dwelling with his people
decisions.reason: The tent word family is used of God's dwelling among Israel in the tabernacle, where his glory filled the tent (Exodus 40:34-35), and of the Word who "tented" among us (John 1:14). Paul may hint that Christ's power dwells with him as God's presence dwelt in the tent. The verb itself does not prove this.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting, as everywhere.

decisions.choice: pitch [its] tent over (L); spread its tent over (B); stay over me like a tent (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the tent in the verb (m2), which "rest upon" loses.

decisions.choice: boast
decisions.reason: As in 12:1, "boast" is kept at every level in these chapters.

decisions.choice: ipige hema (L); itande hema yake (B)
decisions.reason: "Kupiga hema" is the Swahili for pitching a tent, which keeps the Greek picture of coming to dwell and shelter (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "dựng lều trên tôi" (L); "giăng lều che phủ tôi" (B); "ở trên tôi như một cái lều che chở" (R) for episkenoo
decisions.reason: May come to dwell on me and shelter me (m2); the picture of the tent is kept at every level, since it may recall God dwelling with his people (m3, uncertain).

decisions.choice: "장막을 치다" (L); "장막처럼 펼쳐지다" (B); "천막처럼 머물다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as taking up lodging and sheltering; "장막" is the word of 5:1-4 (L, B), "천막" in Readable.

source.text: διὸ εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις, ἐν ὕβρεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν διωγμοῖς καὶ στενοχωρίαις, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ· ὅταν γὰρ ἀσθενῶ, τότε δυνατός εἰμι.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I am well pleased in weaknesses, in insults, in calamities, in persecutions and tight places, for the sake of Christ; whenever for I am weak, then strong I am.

en.L: Therefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in calamities, in persecutions and tight places, for the sake of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; for whenever I am weak, then I am strong.
en.B: That is why I am glad to have weaknesses, insults, calamities, persecutions and tight corners, for the sake of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. For it is when I am weak that I am strong.
en.R: So for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}'s sake I am glad when I am weak, when people insult me, when disasters come, when I am persecuted, and when I feel trapped. For when I am weak, that is when I am strong.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je me plais dans les faiblesses, dans les outrages, dans les calamités, dans les persécutions et les situations sans issue, pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ; car lorsque je suis faible, alors je suis fort.
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi j’accepte avec joie, pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, les faiblesses, les insultes, les calamités, les persécutions et les impasses. Car c’est quand je suis faible que je suis fort.
fr.R: Alors, pour le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, je suis heureux quand je suis faible, quand on m’insulte, quand des malheurs arrivent, quand on me persécute et quand je me sens pris au piège. Car c’est quand je suis faible que je suis fort.

es.L: Por lo cual me complazco en debilidades, en insultos, en necesidades, en persecuciones y angustias, por causa {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}; porque cuando soy débil, entonces soy fuerte.
es.B: Por eso me alegro de tener debilidades, insultos, calamidades, persecuciones y apuros por causa {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Porque cuando soy débil, es cuando soy fuerte.
es.R: Así que, por amor {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}, me alegro cuando soy débil, cuando la gente me insulta, cuando vienen desastres, cuando me persiguen y cuando me siento atrapado. Porque cuando soy débil, es entonces cuando soy fuerte.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo naona furaha katika udhaifu, katika matusi, katika shida, katika madhulumu na mabanio, kwa ajili ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}; kwa maana ninapokuwa dhaifu, ndipo nilipo na nguvu.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu ninafurahi kuwa na udhaifu, matusi, maafa, madhulumu na hali za kubanwa, kwa ajili ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Kwa maana ninapokuwa dhaifu, ndipo ninapokuwa na nguvu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kwa ajili ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ninafurahi ninapokuwa dhaifu, watu wanaponitukana, maafa yanaponipata, ninapoteswa, na ninapojiona nimebanwa pande zote. Kwa maana ninapokuwa dhaifu, ndipo ninapokuwa na nguvu.

vi.L: Vì vậy, tôi vui thích trong những sự yếu đuối, trong những sự sỉ nhục, trong những tai họa, trong những sự bắt bớ và cảnh khốn quẫn, vì cớ {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}; vì khi nào tôi yếu đuối, chính lúc đó tôi mạnh mẽ.
vi.B: Đó là lý do tôi vui lòng chịu những sự yếu đuối, sỉ nhục, tai họa, bắt bớ và những cảnh khốn quẫn, vì cớ {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Vì chính khi tôi yếu đuối là lúc tôi mạnh mẽ.
vi.R: Vậy, vì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, tôi vui lòng khi tôi yếu đuối, khi người ta sỉ nhục tôi, khi tai họa đến, khi tôi bị bắt bớ, và khi tôi thấy mình bị dồn vào đường cùng. Vì khi tôi yếu đuối, chính lúc đó tôi mạnh mẽ.

ko.L: 그러므로 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위하여 약함과 모욕과 궁핍과 박해와 곤경을 기뻐합니다. 내가 약할 때에 그때에 내가 강하기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위해서라면 약함과 모욕과 재난과 박해와 곤경을 기쁘게 받아들입니다. 내가 약할 때에 바로 그때에 내가 강하기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 위해서라면, 내가 약할 때에도, 사람들이 나를 모욕할 때에도, 재난이 닥칠 때에도, 박해를 받을 때에도, 꼼짝할 수 없는 처지에 놓일 때에도 기뻐합니다. 내가 약할 때, 바로 그때에 내가 강하기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: I take pleasure in: I gladly accept, I am content with
alternatives: I enjoy suffering for its own sake
decisions.reason: εὐδοκῶ is to be well pleased with something, to approve it gladly. Paul does not enjoy pain; he welcomes these things because, endured for Christ's sake, they are where Christ's power is at work (verse 9).

decisions.choice: for the sake of Christ: applies to the whole list
decisions.reason: ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ comes at the end and covers every item. These are hardships suffered because Paul serves Christ, not every misfortune.

decisions.choice: insults, calamities, persecutions, tight places
decisions.reason: ὕβρεσιν is insulting, humiliating treatment. ἀνάγκαις is distress or calamity, and στενοχωρίαις is being hemmed in with no way out; both stand in the list of 6:4. διωγμοῖς is persecution for the faith.

decisions.choice: when I am weak, then I am strong: Christ's strength, not Paul's
alternatives: weakness itself is a kind of strength
decisions.reason: The strength is the power of Christ that dwells on Paul (verse 9). His weakness is the place where that power is seen, so the paradox sums up verses 7-10.

decisions.choice: calamities, tight places (L); calamities, tight corners (B); disasters, feel trapped (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as in the list of 6:4, so the two lists can be compared; "hardship" is kept for the word rendered "affliction" at Literal (1:4; 4:17).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: calamités, situations sans issue (L); calamités, impasses (B); des malheurs, pris au piège (R)
decisions.reason: The second word pictures a narrow place with no way out, which "situations sans issue" and "impasses" keep. "Détresse" and "angoisse" name a feeling rather than the situation, and would blur with the word for affliction elsewhere in the letter.

decisions.choice: necesidades, angustias (L); calamidades, apuros (B)
decisions.reason: The same two hardship words as in 6:4, rendered as they are there: Literal keeps the words Spanish has long used, Balanced says disaster and being hemmed in.

decisions.choice: shida, mabanio (L); maafa, hali za kubanwa (B); madhulumu
decisions.reason: Two of these words are in the list of 6:4, so Swahili repeats the words used there. "Madhulumu" (persecutions) keeps "mateso" free for the sufferings of 1:5-7.

decisions.choice: "tai họa", "cảnh khốn quẫn" (L, B); "tai họa đến", "bị dồn vào đường cùng" (R) for anankai and stenochoriai
decisions.reason: Calamities and tight places (m3); "cảnh khốn quẫn" is the word of 6:4 for stenochoria.

decisions.choice: "vui thích" (L); "vui lòng chịu" (B); "vui lòng" (R) for eudokeo
decisions.reason: I gladly accept, I am content with (m1).

decisions.choice: "궁핍", "곤경" (L), as at 6:4; "재난", "곤경" (B); "재난", "꼼짝할 수 없는 처지" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of 6:4 at Literal; the English is "calamities, tight places".

decisions.choice: "기뻐합니다" (L, R); "기쁘게 받아들입니다" (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the verb as gladly accepting, not enjoying suffering.

source.text: Γέγονα ἄφρων· ὑμεῖς με ἠναγκάσατε· ἐγὼ γὰρ ὤφειλον ὑφ’ ὑμῶν συνίστασθαι.

records.literal_gloss: I have become a fool; you me compelled; I for ought by you to be commended.

en.L: I have become a fool; you forced me. For I ought to have been commended by you.
en.B: I have become a fool. You forced me into it. It was you who should have been recommending me.
en.R: I have been acting like a fool. But you made me do it. You should have been the ones recommending me.

fr.L: Je suis devenu insensé ; vous m’y avez contraint. Car moi, j’aurais dû être recommandé par vous.
fr.B: Je suis devenu insensé. C’est vous qui m’y avez obligé. C’était à vous de me recommander.
fr.R: J’ai agi comme un insensé. Mais c’est vous qui m’y avez obligé. C’est vous qui auriez dû me recommander.

es.L: Me he vuelto insensato; {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:obligaron|obligasteis}}. Porque yo debía ser recomendado por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Me he vuelto un insensato. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} me {{plural_you:obligaron|obligasteis}} a ello. {{plural_you:Eran ustedes quienes debían|Erais vosotros quienes debíais}} haberme recomendado.
es.R: He estado actuando como un tonto. Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:obligaron|obligasteis}}. {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{plural_you:debían|debíais}} haber sido los que me recomendaran.

sw.L: Nimekuwa mpumbavu; ninyi mmenilazimisha. Kwa maana ilinipasa kutambulishwa na ninyi.
sw.B: Nimekuwa mpumbavu. Ninyi ndio mlionilazimisha. Ninyi ndio mliopaswa kunitambulisha.
sw.R: Nimekuwa nikitenda kama mpumbavu. Lakini ninyi ndio mlionifanya nifanye hivyo. Ninyi ndio mliopaswa kunisifu kwa wengine.

vi.L: Tôi đã trở nên người ngu dại; anh chị em đã ép buộc tôi. Vì chính anh chị em đáng lẽ phải giới thiệu tôi.
vi.B: Tôi đã trở thành người ngu dại. Chính anh chị em đã buộc tôi phải như vậy. Chính anh chị em mới là những người đáng lẽ phải giới thiệu tôi.
vi.R: Tôi đã hành động như một người ngu dại. Nhưng chính anh chị em đã khiến tôi làm vậy. Anh chị em đáng lẽ phải là những người giới thiệu tôi.

ko.L: 내가 어리석은 사람이 되었습니다. 여러분이 나를 억지로 그렇게 하게 했습니다. 나는 여러분에게서 추천을 받아야 했기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 내가 어리석은 사람이 되었습니다. 여러분이 나를 그렇게 몰아붙였습니다. 나를 추천했어야 할 사람은 바로 여러분이었습니다.
ko.R: 나는 어리석은 사람처럼 행동해 왔습니다. 그러나 여러분이 나를 그렇게 만들었습니다. 나를 추천했어야 할 사람들은 여러분입니다.

decisions.choice: I have become a fool: Paul looks back on his fool's speech
alternatives: Paul admits he is truly foolish
decisions.reason: Γέγονα is perfect: the boasting of 11:16-12:10 is done and stands as said. Paul took on the role of a fool (11:16-17, 21) to answer rivals on their own terms. The word ἄφρων is the same as in 11:16 and 12:6.

decisions.choice: you, emphatic: the Corinthians are to blame
decisions.reason: Both ὑμεῖς ("you") and ἐγὼ ("I") are emphatic. The Corinthians forced him by failing to defend him against the rivals. The imperfect ὤφειλον ("I ought") states what should have happened and did not.

decisions.choice: commended: spoken for, recommended
decisions.reason: συνίστασθαι is the verb of recommendation that runs through the letter (3:1; 4:2; 5:12; 10:12, 18). The Corinthians, who owed their faith to Paul, should have been his letter of recommendation (3:2).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "I have become a fool", with no added word
alternatives: "I have become a fool in boasting"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a participle meaning "boasting" after "fool", which is the reading of the King James Version. The SBLGNT text does not have it. Reviewers must check the manuscript evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a fool (L, B); acting like a fool (R)
decisions.reason: "Fool" keeps the link with the fool's speech of chapter 11 (11:16-19); Readable says that Paul played the part.

decisions.choice: recommending
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "recommend" for this verb, as in 4:2 and chapter 10.

decisions.choice: kutambulishwa (L); kunitambulisha (B); kunisifu (R)
decisions.reason: The commend verb as set in 3:1 and 10:12: "kutambulisha" at Literal and Balanced, "kusifu" at Readable.

decisions.choice: "giới thiệu" for synistemi, as in 3:1 and 10:12-18
decisions.reason: Spoken for, recommended (m3); the book's word, so the theme of self-commendation stays visible.

decisions.choice: "추천을 받다" (L); "추천하다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb of recommendation that runs through the letter (3:1; 5:12; 10:12, 18).

source.text: οὐδὲν γὰρ ὑστέρησα τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων, εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι·

records.literal_gloss: Nothing for I lacked [compared to] the super-extra apostles, if even nothing I am;

en.L: For in nothing did I fall short of the super-apostles, even if I am nothing.
en.B: In nothing did I fall short of these super-apostles, even if I am nothing.
en.R: Those so-called super-apostles are not one bit better than I am, even though I am nothing.

fr.L: Car je n’ai été inférieur en rien aux super-apôtres, même si je ne suis rien.
fr.B: Je n’ai été en rien inférieur à ces super-apôtres, même si je ne suis rien.
fr.R: Ces soi-disant super-apôtres ne valent pas mieux que moi, en rien, même si je ne suis rien.

es.L: Porque en nada fui inferior a los superapóstoles, aunque no soy nada.
es.B: En nada he sido inferior a esos superapóstoles, aunque no soy nada.
es.R: Esos llamados superapóstoles no son mejores que yo en nada, aunque yo no soy nada.

sw.L: Kwa maana sikupungukiwa na kitu kuliko mitume wakuu mno, ingawa mimi si kitu.
sw.B: Sikupungua kwa lolote kuliko hao mitume wakuu mno, hata kama mimi si kitu.
sw.R: Hao wanaoitwa mitume wakuu mno si bora kuliko mimi hata kidogo, ingawa mimi si kitu.

vi.L: Vì tôi chẳng kém gì các siêu sứ đồ, dù tôi chẳng là gì cả.
vi.B: Tôi chẳng thua kém các siêu sứ đồ ấy điều gì, dù tôi chẳng là gì cả.
vi.R: Những người được gọi là siêu sứ đồ ấy chẳng hơn tôi chút nào, dù tôi chẳng là gì cả.

ko.L: 내가 아무것도 아니지만, 나는 그 지극히 뛰어난 사도들보다 조금도 부족하지 않았습니다.
ko.B: 내가 아무것도 아니지만, 나는 이 대단한 사도들보다 조금도 뒤떨어지지 않았습니다.
ko.R: 비록 나는 아무것도 아니지만, 자칭 대단하다는 그 사도들이 나보다 조금도 나을 것이 없습니다.

decisions.choice: the super-apostles: Paul's mocking name for his rivals in Corinth
decisions.reason: ὑπερλίαν means "beyond measure, exceedingly". Paul used the same phrase in 11:5. The phrase mocks people who rate themselves very highly. Most likely they are the rivals of 10:12 and 11:12-15, whom Paul calls false apostles; some think they are the leading apostles in Jerusalem, whose names the rivals invoked. In 11:13 Paul speaks of the rivals in much harsher terms, which some take as a sign that two groups are meant.

decisions.choice: I did not fall short: during his time among them
decisions.reason: ὑστέρησα is aorist and looks back to Paul's ministry in Corinth, which verse 12 goes on to describe.

decisions.choice: even if I am nothing: real humility, with an edge
decisions.reason: εἰ καὶ οὐδέν εἰμι means "even though I am nothing". In himself Paul claims nothing (1 Corinthians 3:7; 15:9-10), and what he is he owes to grace. At the same time the phrase turns the rivals' scorn back on them: if he is nothing, they are less.

decisions.choice: super-apostles (L, B); those so-called super-apostles (R)
decisions.reason: "Super-apostles" keeps the mocking tone of the phrase (m1). Readable adds "so-called" so a young reader sees that Paul is using their own high opinion of themselves, in the same words as 11:5.

decisions.choice: les super-apôtres (L, B); ces soi-disant super-apôtres (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, "super-apôtres" keeps the mocking tone of Paul's phrase (m1); "par excellence" sounds like praise. Readable adds "soi-disant" so the irony is plain, in the same words as 11:5.

decisions.choice: "các siêu sứ đồ" (L); "các siêu sứ đồ ấy" (B); "Những người được gọi là siêu sứ đồ ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 11:5: Paul's mocking name for his rivals (m1, uncertain).

decisions.choice: The name of 11:5: "그 지극히 뛰어난 사도들" (L); "이 대단한 사도들" (B); "자칭 대단하다는 그 사도들" (R)
decisions.reason: Paul's mocking name for his rivals, kept the same as at 11:5.

decisions.choice: "내가 아무것도 아니지만" placed first
decisions.reason: Korean puts a concessive clause before the main clause.

source.text: τὰ μὲν σημεῖα τοῦ ἀποστόλου κατειργάσθη ἐν ὑμῖν ἐν πάσῃ ὑπομονῇ, σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ δυνάμεσιν.

records.literal_gloss: The indeed signs of the apostle were worked among you in all endurance, by signs both and wonders and powerful deeds.

en.L: The signs of the apostle were indeed performed among you in all endurance, by signs and wonders and powerful deeds.
en.B: Among you, with all endurance, the signs that mark an apostle were done: signs, wonders and deeds of power.
en.R: The signs that prove someone is an apostle were done among you. I kept going patiently through everything, and there were signs, wonders and miracles.

fr.L: Les signes de l’apôtre ont certes été accomplis parmi vous en toute endurance, par des signes, des prodiges et des actions puissantes.
fr.B: Les signes qui marquent un apôtre ont été accomplis parmi vous avec une parfaite endurance : signes, prodiges et actes de puissance.
fr.R: Les signes qui prouvent que quelqu’un est apôtre ont été faits parmi vous. J’ai tenu bon patiemment en toutes circonstances, et il y a eu des signes, des prodiges et des miracles.

es.L: Las señales del apóstol, en verdad, fueron hechas entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con toda perseverancia, con señales, prodigios y obras poderosas.
es.B: Entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, con toda perseverancia, se hicieron las señales que distinguen a un apóstol: señales, prodigios y obras poderosas.
es.R: Las señales que demuestran que alguien es apóstol se hicieron entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Yo seguí adelante con paciencia en todo, y hubo señales, maravillas y milagros.

sw.L: Ishara za mtume kweli zilitendwa kati yenu katika uvumilivu wote, kwa ishara na maajabu na matendo ya nguvu.
sw.B: Kati yenu, kwa uvumilivu wote, ishara zinazoonyesha mtume halisi zilitendeka: ishara, maajabu na matendo ya nguvu.
sw.R: Ishara zinazothibitisha kwamba mtu ni mtume zilifanyika kati yenu. Niliendelea kuvumilia katika kila hali, na kulikuwa na ishara, maajabu na miujiza.

vi.L: Thật vậy, các dấu hiệu của sứ đồ đã được thực hiện giữa anh chị em trong mọi sự kiên trì, bằng các dấu lạ, các điều kỳ diệu và các việc quyền năng.
vi.B: Giữa anh chị em, với tất cả sự kiên trì, những dấu hiệu chứng tỏ một sứ đồ đã được thực hiện: các dấu lạ, các điều kỳ diệu và các việc quyền năng.
vi.R: Những dấu hiệu chứng tỏ một người là sứ đồ đã được thực hiện giữa anh chị em. Tôi đã kiên trì chịu đựng mọi điều, và đã có những dấu lạ, những điều kỳ diệu và những phép lạ.

ko.L: 사도의 표징들이 모든 인내로 여러분 가운데서 이루어졌습니다. 곧 표징들과 기사들과 능력 있는 일들로 [이루어졌습니다].
ko.B: 여러분 가운데서 온갖 인내로 사도임을 보여 주는 표징들이 행해졌습니다. 곧 표징들과 기사들과 능력 있는 일들입니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 사도라는 것을 증명하는 표징들이 여러분 가운데서 일어났습니다. 나는 모든 것을 참고 꿋꿋이 견뎠습니다. 그리고 표징들과 놀라운 일들과 기적들이 있었습니다.

decisions.choice: the signs of the apostle: the marks that show a true apostle
decisions.reason: The article in τοῦ ἀποστόλου is generic: "the apostle" is any true apostle. The first σημεῖα are the evidences of apostleship; the end of the sentence names the miracles among them.

decisions.choice: were performed: done among them, by God through Paul
alternatives: Paul performed them by his own power
decisions.reason: The passive κατειργάσθη lets Paul avoid saying "I did". In Romans 15:18-19 he speaks of what Christ worked through him "by the power of signs and wonders".

decisions.choice: indeed: the sentence implies "but you did not take notice"
decisions.reason: μὲν usually looks ahead to a contrasting "but". None follows, and the unspoken contrast is the Corinthians' failure to recognize what they had seen, which leads into verse 13.

decisions.choice: endurance: perseverance under hardship
decisions.reason: ὑπομονῇ is the endurance of 1:6 and 6:4. The signs were done in the middle of hardship, which fits the weakness Paul has just boasted of.

decisions.choice: signs, wonders and deeds of power: three words for miracles
decisions.reason: The three words often go together (Acts 2:22; Romans 15:19). A sign points beyond itself, a wonder astonishes, and a deed of power shows God's might; the same events can be all three.

decisions.choice: signs
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and is kept for both uses, even where the first means "evidences" (m1).

decisions.choice: powerful deeds (L); deeds of power (B); miracles (R)
decisions.reason: δυνάμεσιν is the plural of the word for power, here acts of power; Readable uses the everyday word.

decisions.choice: I kept going patiently through everything
decisions.reason: Readable says whose endurance is meant: Paul's, during his time among them.

decisions.choice: matendo ya nguvu (L, B); miujiza (R); ishara, maajabu
decisions.reason: As in Romans 15:19, "ishara na maajabu" (signs and wonders); the third word is "matendo ya nguvu" (deeds of power) at Literal and Balanced and "miujiza" at Readable, as the settled New Testament terms have it.

decisions.choice: "các dấu hiệu của sứ đồ" (L); "những dấu hiệu chứng tỏ một sứ đồ" (B, R) for the first semeia; "các dấu lạ" for the second
decisions.reason: The marks that show a true apostle (m1), then miracles (m5); Vietnamese has two words, so "dấu hiệu" names the marks and "dấu lạ" the miracles.

decisions.choice: "các dấu lạ, các điều kỳ diệu và các việc quyền năng" (L, B); "những dấu lạ, những điều kỳ diệu và những phép lạ" (R)
decisions.reason: Three words for miracles (m5); "dấu lạ và điều kỳ diệu" is the pair of the Vietnamese Romans 15:19.

decisions.choice: "sự kiên trì" (L, B); "kiên trì chịu đựng" (R) for hypomone
decisions.reason: Perseverance under hardship (m4); as in 1:6 and 6:4.

decisions.choice: "표징, 기사, 능력 있는 일" (L, B); "표징, 놀라운 일, 기적" (R)
